title: MolDx and the technical assessment process
scope: How MolDx works — Palmetto's role, the dossier process, technical assessment vs coverage decisions, the timeline from dossier to LCD.
why: MolDx coverage is often the gating event for molecular dx commercial viability. Investors price it in heavily.
questions: How long does the average dossier-to-LCD cycle take? What's the approval rate? Which MAC jurisdictions matter most by volume? What recent MolDx decisions have moved markets?

title: MAC LCDs vs NCDs vs commercial coverage
scope: The hierarchy — national vs local coverage, how MACs differ, how commercial payers respond to CMS decisions.
why: Coverage strategy determines launch sequencing. Some companies chase NCDs; others run MAC-by-MAC.
questions: What's the typical lag from CMS coverage to commercial follow-on? Which commercial payers lead vs lag? What's the strategic case for chasing an NCD vs accumulating LCDs?

title: CPT vs PLA codes; gap-fill vs cross-walk pricing
scope: AMA's CPT process, the PLA (Proprietary Laboratory Analyses) carve-out, how gap-fill pricing works through the contractor's "reasonable" determination vs cross-walking to existing codes.
why: Pricing is determined as much by code strategy as by clinical utility. Gap-fill can produce 3-5x ASP differences.
questions: What's the typical gap-fill cycle and how often do prices reset? Which dx companies have played this game well? What's the case for PLA vs Category I?

title: ADLT (Advanced Diagnostic Laboratory Test) designation
scope: PAMA's ADLT carveout, the qualifying criteria, the temporary pricing protections, the new ADLT applications recently approved.
why: ADLT pricing protects launch economics for ~9 months. It's one of the few payer-side advantages a sole-source dx can secure.
questions: How many ADLTs have been granted in the last 24 months? What's the typical ASP delta vs cross-walk? What are the renewal dynamics?

title: Z-codes and the role they play in claims
scope: What Z-codes are (DEX Z-Code identifiers), how they're issued, why payers require them, the practical workflow for billing.
why: Z-codes are the operational layer of MolDx coverage. No Z-code, no claim. Many startups underestimate this.
questions: What's the Z-code application process timeline? Which payers require them beyond MolDx? How do Z-codes interact with PLA codes?

title: Prior authorization economics
scope: PA burden — labor cost per claim, denial rates, appeal economics, the dx companies that have made PA reduction a strategic moat.
why: PA can consume 5-15% of revenue in operational cost and 10-25% in lost claims. It's the silent killer of dx unit economics.
questions: Who tracks PA denial rates publicly? What's the appeal-to-overturn ratio in molecular dx? Which dx companies have built PA-bypass workflows?

title: Patient cost-share and assistance economics
scope: How patient out-of-pocket exposure shapes test volume, the role of patient assistance programs, the strategic decision to absorb cost-share.
why: Cost-share suppression is a real volume driver. Dx companies that absorb it grow faster but burn more.
questions: What's the patient OOP threshold above which order rates collapse? How do PAPs interact with anti-kickback rules? What's the ROI math on cost-share absorption?

title: Hospital outreach billing vs outpatient billing
scope: The difference between dx revenue captured via hospital outpatient reimbursement (APC bundles) vs sendout outpatient lab billing.
why: Same test, very different revenue. This is why some dx strategies focus on AMC channel vs national reference labs.
questions: What's the typical revenue delta? How do hospital lab outreach programs structure pricing for their physicians? Where does Mayo Reference fit in this stack?

title: LDT Final Rule status and the IVCT alternative
scope: Where the FDA Final Rule stands today (litigation, enforcement discretion, phase-in), the IVCT legislative path, and what each scenario means commercially.
why: This determines whether LDTs continue or whether everything shifts to FDA pathways. The investor pricing differs by ~10x.
questions: What's the current litigation status? What enforcement discretion has FDA signaled? What's the IVCT path's realistic timeline?

title: FDA pathways for IVDs — 510(k), De Novo, PMA, Breakthrough
scope: The four main pathways, when each applies, typical timelines, costs, and the strategic implications for venture-backed dx.
why: Pathway choice can be a 3-year delta in time-to-market and a $10M+ delta in cost.
questions: What's the current 510(k) cycle time for molecular IVDs? How many breakthrough designations have gone to dx in the last 24 months? What's the realistic De Novo timeline?

title: CLIA — high complexity, moderate, waived
scope: The CLIA tier system, the operational requirements at each tier, the strategic role of CLIA-waived tests in PoC dynamics.
why: Moving from high-complexity to waived can 10x a test's addressable market — but takes years of clinical evidence.
questions: How many tests have moved from high-complexity to waived in the last 3 years? What's the typical evidence package required? Who are the reference operators for waived dx?

title: CAP accreditation and proficiency testing
scope: CAP's role, the inspection cycle, what proficiency testing covers, the operational implications for new entrants.
why: CAP issues are operational killers. Lab consolidations often unwind because of CAP-related findings.
questions: What CAP findings most commonly drive remediation? How does CAP intersect with FDA for IVDs? What's the practical cost of CAP non- compliance?

title: NY CLEP and other state-level approvals
scope: New York's separate clinical lab approval system, why it exists, which other states have meaningful approval requirements.
why: NY CLEP can delay launch in NY by 6-18 months. For some dx categories, NY is 8-12% of national volume.
questions: What's the current CLEP cycle time? Which dx categories get flagged most? Which states beyond NY matter (WA, FL, CA)?

title: ISO 15189 in the lab
scope: International accreditation, when it matters (mostly export and pharma partnerships), how it relates to CAP.
why: For dx companies pursuing global pharma partnerships, ISO 15189 is often a precondition.
questions: How many U.S. dx labs hold ISO 15189? What's the typical certification cost?

title: Quality systems for IVDs (QSR / 21 CFR 820 / ISO 13485)
scope: The quality system architecture that's required for FDA-cleared IVDs, how it differs from LDT operations.
why: Many LDT-first dx companies hit a wall when transitioning to FDA pathways because their quality systems weren't designed for it.
questions: What's the typical cost to retrofit a QSR system onto an LDT operation? Where do most companies fail in their first IVD audit?

title: How a test enters major society guidelines (NCCN, IDSA, KDIGO, AGA, AAN, ASCO)
scope: The actual mechanics — how panels work, what evidence packages they require, the difference between Category 1, 2A, 2B in NCCN, etc.
why: Guideline inclusion is often the inflection point for test volume. It also unlocks reimbursement via medical necessity.
questions: What's the typical evidence package? How long from publication to guideline update? Which societies move fastest vs slowest?

title: KOL networks and their role in adoption
scope: How dx companies build KOL networks, the difference between paid speakers and unpaid champions, the role of KOLs in payer dossiers.
why: A test without 5-10 strong KOL champions struggles to cross from launch to mainstream adoption.
questions: How do successful dx companies structure their KOL programs? What's the strategic difference between hub-and-spoke vs distributed networks?

title: EMR ordering — order set economics, decision support, friction
scope: How tests get into Epic / Cerner order sets, what governance bodies decide, the role of CDS rules.
why: Tests that aren't in the order set get ordered ~10x less often than tests that are. EMR integration is invisible but determinative.
questions: What's the typical Epic-integration timeline? Who at the health system actually approves order set changes? What CDS levers exist?

title: Lab director psychology — sendout vs in-house decisions
scope: How lab medical directors decide what to bring in-house, the role of volume thresholds, equipment amortization, staffing.
why: Sendout-to-in-house decisions are massive volume shifts for dx companies. Predicting them is alpha.
questions: What volume threshold typically triggers in-house assessment? What CapEx is required? How do lab directors weigh strategic vs financial?

title: Reference lab channel — Quest, LabCorp, ARUP, Mayo, Bioreference
scope: How sendout works, who controls volume, the contracting dynamics, why some dx companies sell direct vs through reference labs.
why: Reference labs have huge gravitational pull on test volume. Companies that crack their channel scale faster.
questions: What's the typical reference lab contract structure? Who at Quest / LabCorp / ARUP makes inclusion decisions? What's Mayo Reference's strategic position?

title: Hospital-based outreach programs
scope: AMC and community hospital lab outreach — Mayo's MCS, ARUP's channel, hospital-system reference operations.
why: Hospital outreach is a different revenue model than reference lab sendout. Margins, contracting, and customer dynamics differ.
questions: What % of national lab volume runs through hospital outreach vs reference? How does this differ by dx category?

title: Direct-to-consumer dynamics
scope: DTC dx (Cologuard, Galleri), the marketing economics, the prescription requirements, the FTC/state regulatory layer.
why: DTC bypasses ordering friction but creates new pressures (CAC, prescription handling, telehealth integration).
questions: What's the typical DTC CAC for screening dx? Which states block what? What's the conversion-to-prescription rate?

title: Companion diagnostics and pharma-driven dx
scope: How CDx gets developed, the FDA-pharma codevelopment pathway, the economics of CDx vs broader IVD.
why: CDx revenue is often guaranteed by pharma at launch but capped. The strategic question is when to broaden beyond CDx.
questions: What's the typical CDx revenue per drug? What's the time from drug approval to CDx commoditization? Which CDx have escaped to broader use?

title: Sample volume to break-even
scope: The unit-economics math — fixed bioinformatics + lab capacity, variable per-sample cost, the volume curve to gross-margin positivity.
why: Most dx companies misjudge their break-even by 2-3x. Burn rate visibility depends on this.
questions: What's the typical break-even volume for an NGS-based dx? How does it differ for PCR-based, mass-spec-based, etc.?

title: ASP dynamics over the test lifecycle
scope: How ASP evolves — initial ADLT or gap-fill, payer mix shift, out-of-network compression, eventual cross-walk to commodity.
why: ASP is rarely flat. Compression timelines determine enterprise value.
questions: What's the typical ASP curve over 5 years? Which test categories are most resistant to compression?

title: COGS — reagents, instruments, labor, sample logistics
scope: The cost stack — what % goes where, where compression is possible, where it isn't.
why: COGS architecture determines who can compete on price and who must compete on differentiation.
questions: What's the typical COGS breakdown for NGS, PCR, mass-spec, immunoassay-based dx? Where does sample logistics dominate?

title: Volume-vs-price tradeoffs
scope: When to accept lower ASP for higher volume (commercial vs Medicare strategy), the elasticity of demand for dx.
why: Most dx companies default to "high ASP, low volume" and never question it.
questions: Which dx companies have successfully traded ASP for volume? What's the inflection point in volume that justifies it?

title: Bioinformatics infrastructure as fixed cost
scope: The one-time and ongoing cost of bioinformatics — pipeline development, validation, maintenance, scaling.
why: Bioinformatics is often the under-budgeted line item. It also determines how fast a company can iterate.
questions: What's the typical bioinformatics headcount per assay? What fraction of dx engineering is regulatory-driven vs feature-driven?

title: Distribution — in-house lab vs partnership vs licensing
scope: The three main distribution models, when each makes sense, the margin implications.
why: Distribution choice is often irreversible. Companies that pick the wrong model spend years repositioning.
questions: What's the margin delta across the three models? Which dx categories favor which model?

title: Burn rate dynamics in dx companies
scope: How dx burn rates compare to therapeutics, devices, software. The major burn drivers and their compression levers.
why: Investors evaluate burn against revenue trajectory. Dx burn norms are very different from therapeutic norms.
questions: What's the typical burn rate for a clinical-stage dx? Pre-launch? Post-launch? What's the burn-multiple benchmark?

title: First-mover vs fast-follower in dx
scope: When first-mover advantage holds (network-effect dx, KOL-tied dx) vs when fast-followers win (commodity assays, technically routine).
why: Investment thesis depends on which side of this you're on.
questions: Which dx categories are first-mover-protected vs not? Examples of fast-followers winning?

title: Commoditization curves — what protects vs erodes
scope: What makes a dx defensible long-term — IP, operational moat, network effects, KOL relationships, payer contracts.
why: Most dx commoditize within 5-7 years. Which won't?
questions: What's the typical commoditization timeline? Which moats hold longest?

title: IP moats vs operational moats
scope: Patent protection in dx (limited), trade-secret protection (stronger), the operational moat of a working lab + KOL network + payer contracts.
why: Investors over-weight IP and under-weight operational moats. The latter often matters more.
questions: How many dx companies have lost on IP litigation? What's the strategic case for trade-secret over patent?

title: Multiplex strategies and cannibalization
scope: When multiplex panels cannibalize singleton tests (sometimes good for the company, sometimes bad), the strategic decision points.
why: Multiplex shifts ASP and margins. The math isn't obvious.
questions: When do payers reimburse multiplex above the sum of singletons? When do they reimburse below?

title: Platform plays vs single-test plays
scope: The strategic difference — building a platform that supports many assays vs commercializing one assay deeply.
why: Platform plays raise differently and exit differently than single-test plays.
questions: Which dx companies have successfully transitioned from single-test to platform?

title: How acquirers value dx assets
scope: Strategic acquirers' valuation models — revenue multiples, technology multiples, strategic-fit premia, channel-fit premia.
why: Exit strategy depends on understanding what acquirers pay for and why.
questions: What revenue multiples have recent dx M&A printed at? What strategic-fit premia have been observable?

scope: What motivates them, what frictions they face, what they read, who influences them, and what gets them to change ordering behavior.
